item.title: scim — provisioning people and groups from an identity provider
item.description:
Who has the identity provider just created, changed or deleted? An identity provider (Entra ID, Okta, Keycloak, …) creates, updates and deletes people and groups in your application over HTTP; this package is that HTTP endpoint, for Users and Groups (RFC 7643, RFC 7644), over a Backend you write. Pure Go, CGO_ENABLED=0, standard library only.

go get github.com/go-authn/scim@v0.2.0

Example 

srv := &scim.Server{
 Backend: scim.NewMemory(), // or your database
 BaseURL: "https://app.example.org/scim/v2", // for meta.location
}
mux.Handle("/scim/v2/", http.StripPrefix("/scim/v2", scim.BearerAuth(token, srv)))

The Server assigns ids, timestamps and versions, validates input and applies PATCH; the Backend keeps what it is given and enforces what only it can see:ErrConflict for a taken userName (409 uniqueness), InvalidValue for a member that does not exist (400 invalidValue), ErrPrecondition when the stored version is not the one that was read. NewMemory() is the reference implementation.

It serves /Users and /Groups (list with filter, startIndex, count,attributes, excludedAttributes; create; get, PUT, PATCH and DELETE by id with ETag and If-Match), /Users/.search and /Groups/.search, and the discovery endpoints /ServiceProviderConfig, /ResourceTypes and /Schemas.Filters cover the whole grammar of RFC 7644 §3.4.2.2; PATCH is atomic: an operation that fails leaves the resource as it was.

What it refuses, and why

Everything here comes from outside, so the limits are part of the API:
a body over MaxBodyBytes (1 MiB), a PATCH with more than MaxOperations (100), or one that grows the resource past the body limit 413
a group with more than MaxMembers (10 000) 400 invalidValue
a filter over 4 KiB, nested deeper than 32, with an unknown operator, or gt on a boolean 400 invalidFilter
writes to id, meta, schemas or a user’s groups 400 mutability
a resource without its core schema, a userName that is empty, over 256 bytes or has control characters, two primary emails 400
a missing or wrong bearer token (BearerAuth, constant time; an empty token admits nobody) 401
any Backend error that is not one of the sentinels 500 with a body that says nothing; the error goes to ErrorLog

Not supported: bulk operations, sorting, password changes, /Me (announced as such in /ServiceProviderConfig).

What v0.2.0 changed

From an audit, a fuzzing and chaos pass and a performance pass. What a caller can see:

  • Server.ReadTimeout, new, default 30 s: a request body that takes longer to arrive is cut off with a 400. It replaces the http.Server’s ownReadTimeout for the request; a negative value leaves the http.Server’s alone.
  • ConditionalDeleter, a new optional interface a Backend may implement(DeleteUserIf, DeleteGroupIf), which Memory does. DELETE withIf-Match used to check the version and delete in two steps, so a write landing between them was deleted unseen.
  • A lost race is redone. A PATCH or PUT without If-Match that lost a race with another writer was answered 412 although the client asked for no precondition; it is now redone on the newer version, at most 32 times. WithIf-Match the answer is still 412. Of 24 concurrent PATCHes withoutIf-Match, 9 failed with 412 before and none now.
  • Removing a member, or any element, through a filter that matches nothing succeeds; it was a 400 noTarget (RFC 7644 §3.5.2.2).
  • A PATCH without a path applies its keys in sorted order; it used the map’s order, so name and name.givenName in one object gave a different resource from run to run.
  • BearerAuth accepts the scheme name in any case (bearer <token>, RFC 7235§2.1).
  • startIndex and count are clamped whatever the size of an int: a value beyond it was a 400 on 32-bit targets and a clamped page on 64-bit ones.
  • A Filter.Equality() hands a Backend the decoded string. It is data: pass it to the database as a parameter, and never splice it into a query.

Bulk operations, sorting and password changes remain unsupported.

Allocations of one list request over 10,000 users and 200 groups onMemory, exact, from go test -bench, Apple M4 Max:

list request before after
a page of 100 789,417 allocations, 47.7 MB 14,952 allocations, 6.0 MB
userName eq 797,979 allocations, 47.7 MB 90 allocations, 12.6 KB
a filter that scans every user (name.givenName eq and emails[...]) 818,847 allocations, 48 MB 361,098 allocations, 29.7 MB

Wall-clock was not measured: the load was 65, and the rule is under 9. The noisy single runs (about 1.7 s to 0.06 s for the scanning filter) are not a result.FuzzPatchPath, FuzzPatchThenDecode, FuzzFilter and FuzzServer ran 45 s each with 16 workers, 1.3 to 2.4 million executions, and found no failure.

What it is checked against

What identity providers really send, tested with their payloads: Entra ID’s "Replace", its string booleans ("active": "False"), its member removal by value list, its filtered add that creates an email; Okta’s replace without a path that repeats the id. The filter, PATCH and the whole handler are fuzzed(FuzzFilter, FuzzPatch, FuzzServer), and the coverage lane’s floor is 92%.

Reference

pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-authn/scim@v0.2.0
